title: Repair NATIVE_COMPUTE_CORE canonical directory row stale Python semantics
summary: Human-governor finding 2026-10-02: the canonical project_architecture_directory row for NATIVE_COMPUTE_CORE still carries pre-retirement semantics — failure_boundary 'native dispatch falls back to the Python path (B38/E184)' and runtime_boundary 'borrowed pointers only; Python owns all memory (B40/E186)'. This contradicts the current codex itself: B73 abolishes every Python role and residency, B38/E184 define the native-unavailable contract as last-verified owner-language path or fail-closed with PYTHON-FALLBACK:none, B40/E186 define only the C ABI and physical layout (no memory owner is stated), and B166/B74 allocate ownership to registered owner languages. Corrected text: failure_boundary cites the owner-language-or-fail-closed contract with no Python fallback; runtime_boundary assigns memory ownership to the loading process/owning engine (per OBL_NATIVE_COMPUTE_CORE_CLASS acceptance 'runtime-owner=loading-process-or-owning-engine'). The a233_normalized_directory_entry projection of the same row is updated in the same revision so canonical and projection never diverge. Codex-only change: no implementation is modified.
origin: direct human-governor finding 2026-10-02: 現在不是 A233 stale，而是 canonical directory 本身有舊語意 — NATIVE_COMPUTE_CORE current row 還寫 'native dispatch falls back to Python' 與 'Python owns all memory'，與 B38/B74 Python zero-role/zero-fallback 衝突。

problem.summary: Canonical project_architecture_directory NATIVE_COMPUTE_CORE row retains retired-Python semantics in failure_boundary and runtime_boundary; the A233 normalized projection faithfully mirrors the same stale text, so the defect is in the canonical row, not the projection.

changes.proposed: native dispatch falls back only to a last-verified owner-language path or fails closed; Python fallback none (B38/E184/B73)
borrowed pointers only; memory owned by the loading process or owning engine (B40/B166)
